items.stem: A new switch uplink creates an intermittent broadcast storm. Which protocol is designed to prevent the Layer 2 loop causing it?

options.rationale: Correct: STP blocks redundant paths to prevent Layer 2 loops.
BGP is a Layer 3 path-vector protocol, not a loop-prevention mechanism for bridging.
DHCP assigns addresses and does not prevent bridging loops.
SNMP is for monitoring, not loop prevention.

items.explanation: Correct: STP blocks redundant paths to prevent Layer 2 loops.

items.stem: To prefer one upstream ISP for outbound traffic within your AS, which BGP attribute is most appropriate?

options.rationale: Correct: local preference is the standard way to influence outbound path selection AS-wide.
MED influences how a neighbour AS sends traffic to you, not your outbound choice.
Origin is a low-priority tiebreaker, not the primary outbound control.
Router ID is a final tiebreaker, not a policy control.

items.explanation: Correct: local preference is the standard way to influence outbound path selection AS-wide.

items.stem: Which TWO controls harden an untrusted access-layer port? (Select TWO)

options.text: Port security limiting learned MAC addresses
options.rationale: Correct: port security limits MACs to curb spoofing and CAM flooding.

options.text: Storm control to cap broadcast/multicast rates
options.rationale: Correct: storm control limits broadcast/multicast floods.

options.text: Enabling an unauthenticated trunk to all VLANs
options.rationale: An open trunk exposes every VLAN and weakens security.

options.text: Disabling spanning tree on the port
options.rationale: Disabling STP invites loops rather than hardening the port.

items.explanation: Correct: port security limits MACs to curb spoofing and CAM flooding. Correct: storm control limits broadcast/multicast floods.
